versions.label: Steam Linux (build 26445667)
versions.notes: Native x86-64 Steam Linux build, run by Android FEX 2610 directly (no PRoot) through the app's direct FEX bridge, with the Turnip Gen8 V37 driver on Adreno 8xx. The bridge's Counter-Strike 2 entry carries the rest: FEX TSO emulation (without it the game dies at start), the Vulkan subgroup repair preload, a host-side pool allocator (keeps Turnip's ~30,000 retained 32 KiB slabs under vm.max_map_count), the browser-socket fallback and /root mapped to the Linux home. The profile turns on the thread pinning that gave the most: all 8 cores, the game's main and render threads on the prime cores, the other threads on the rest (perfPrimeCores), plus thread priority. Measured on a Redmagic Astra 2 (SM8850P, Adreno 840, Android 16, AC power, 79-92% battery), de_dust2 casual without bots, 640x480, lowest graphics, 180 s of scripted play: about 99-109 fps with all cores and no pinning, 124 fps (30 s windows 118-125) pinned, with no frame over 17 ms. In a busy online Deathmatch (about 14 players) one screenshot showed 72 fps, so that case is not tuned. Turnip sysmem/gmem, a lower resolution and the high-refresh preference did not change the ~124 fps ceiling beyond run-to-run noise (the baseline alone swung 117-124). Known problems: the game exits at start with code 139 ('Failed writing minidump') on about every second launch; launch again. Needs the app build with the physical-mouse fixes for a mouse to turn the camera. A low battery slows the tablet sharply: keep it charged.

versions.label: Other Linux builds
versions.notes: Only Steam build 26445667 was tested. Valve updates the game often and the bridge's patches (library names, startup path) may need changes for a newer build; these defaults are not verification of other builds.
